title: Coxinha
shortDescription: Brazilian chicken croquettes with a creamy shredded chicken filling and crispy coating
note: Shape into teardrop forms for authentic presentation
introCopy: These iconic Brazilian street food snacks feature tender shredded chicken enveloped in a smooth dough, breaded and fried until golden. The name means 'little thigh' due to their traditional shape.

steps.text: Poach chicken breasts in water for 20 minutes until cooked through. Cool and shred finely.
Heat olive oil in a pan and sauté onion and garlic until soft. Add shredded chicken, cream cheese, salt, and pepper. Mix until creamy and set aside to cool completely.
For the dough, bring chicken stock, butter, and salt to a boil. Remove from heat and add all the flour at once, stirring vigorously until a smooth dough forms.
Knead the dough on a clean surface for 2-3 minutes until smooth. Let rest for 10 minutes.
Take a small portion of dough, flatten it in your palm, place a spoonful of filling in the center, and shape into a teardrop (chicken thigh shape). Repeat with remaining dough and filling.
Dip each coxinha in beaten egg, then roll in breadcrumbs to coat completely.
Heat oil to 180°C (350°F) and deep-fry coxinhas in batches until golden brown, about 4-5 minutes. Drain on paper towels.
Serve hot with your choice of hot sauce or ketchup.

title: Brigadeiro
shortDescription: Classic Brazilian chocolate truffle made with condensed milk and cocoa powder
note: Roll while still slightly warm for best texture
introCopy: Brazil's most beloved sweet treat, these fudgy chocolate balls are a staple at every birthday party and celebration. Simple ingredients transform into irresistible confections.

steps.text: In a medium saucepan, combine condensed milk, cocoa powder, butter, and salt. Mix well.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon, until the mixture thickens and starts to pull away from the bottom of the pan, about 10-12 minutes.
Transfer to a greased plate and let cool for 30 minutes until you can handle it.
Grease your hands with butter and roll tablespoon-sized portions into balls.
Roll each ball in chocolate sprinkles to coat completely. Place in mini paper cups if desired.
Refrigerate until ready to serve. Best served at room temperature.

title: Acarajé
shortDescription: Bahian black-eyed pea fritters filled with vatapá and shrimp
note: Traditional street food from Salvador, Bahia
introCopy: This iconic Afro-Brazilian street food features crispy fried black-eyed pea fritters split and filled with a spicy shrimp paste. A taste of Bahia's rich cultural heritage.

steps.text: Drain soaked black-eyed peas and rub between hands to remove skins. Rinse well.
Blend peas with onion and salt in a food processor until a smooth, thick paste forms. Beat the mixture for 3-4 minutes to incorporate air.

For the filling, heat oil and sauté onion and garlic until soft. Add prawns, tomatoes, ginger, pepper, and salt. Cook for 5 minutes, then add coconut milk and simmer until thickened, about 10 minutes.
Heat oil to 180°C (350°F). Using two spoons, shape bean paste into oval patties and carefully drop into hot oil. Fry until golden brown, about 5 minutes per batch.
Drain fritters on paper towels. While still warm, cut each one partially open like a pita pocket.
Fill each acarajé with a generous spoonful of the shrimp mixture. Serve immediately.

title: Farofa Completa
shortDescription: Rich toasted cassava flour with bacon, vegetables, and eggs
note: Essential accompaniment to feijoada and grilled meats
introCopy: This elaborate version of Brazil's beloved toasted cassava flour side dish is loaded with bacon, sausage, vegetables, and hard-boiled eggs. A feast in itself.

steps.text: In a large skillet, cook bacon over medium heat until crispy. Remove and set aside, leaving fat in pan.
Add sausage to the same pan and cook until browned. Remove and set aside.
In the remaining fat, sauté onion and garlic until soft. Add carrot and green beans, cooking until just tender, about 5 minutes.
Add butter to the pan. Once melted, gradually add cassava flour, stirring constantly to toast evenly until golden and fragrant, about 8-10 minutes.
Return bacon and sausage to the pan. Add chopped eggs, olives, and parsley. Mix well and season with salt and pepper.
Adjust seasoning if needed. Serve warm as a side dish.

title: Bobó de Camarão
shortDescription: Creamy cassava and coconut shrimp stew from Bahia
note: Serve with white rice and farofa
introCopy: This luxurious Bahian dish blends cassava (yuca) into a velvety purée enriched with coconut milk and studded with succulent shrimp. Comfort food from Brazil's northeast coast.

steps.text: Boil cassava in salted water until very tender, about 25-30 minutes. Drain and mash or blend until smooth.
Season prawns with lime juice, salt, and pepper. Set aside for 15 minutes.
Heat oil in a large pan and sauté onion and garlic until golden. Add bell pepper and tomatoes, cooking until softened, about 8 minutes.
Add the mashed cassava and coconut milk to the pan, stirring until well combined and creamy. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Add prawns and cook until they turn pink and are cooked through, about 5 minutes.
Stir in fresh coriander and adjust seasoning. Serve hot over white rice with farofa on the side.

title: Vatapá
shortDescription: Creamy Bahian bread and nut paste with shrimp and coconut
note: Traditional filling for acarajé or served with rice
introCopy: This rich, thick paste from Bahia blends bread, shrimp, peanuts, cashews, and coconut milk into a complex, aromatic dish that showcases African-Brazilian culinary heritage.

steps.text: Blend soaked bread (squeezed of excess water), peanuts, cashews, and dried shrimp with 200ml water until smooth. Set aside.
Heat oil in a large pan and sauté onion and garlic until soft. Add tomatoes, ginger, and pepper, cooking for 5 minutes.
Add the blended nut mixture to the pan and stir well. Cook for 5 minutes.
Add coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer. Cook, stirring frequently, until the mixture thickens to a creamy paste consistency, about 15-20 minutes.
Add fresh prawns and cook until pink and cooked through, about 5 minutes.
Stir in coriander and adjust salt. Serve hot with white rice or as a filling for acarajé.

title: Pastel de Carne
shortDescription: Crispy deep-fried pastries filled with seasoned ground beef
note: Brazil's favorite street snack, best eaten hot
introCopy: These golden, flaky half-moon pastries are found at every Brazilian street fair and market. The thin, crispy dough shatters to reveal a savory beef filling.

steps.text: For the dough, mix flour and salt in a bowl. Add oil and warm water, kneading until smooth and elastic, about 8 minutes. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.

For the filling, brown ground beef in a pan over medium-high heat. Add onion and garlic, cooking until soft. Add tomato, tomato paste, cumin, salt, pepper, and parsley. Cook until liquid evaporates, about 10 minutes. Cool completely.
Roll dough very thin (2mm) and cut into circles about 10cm in diameter using a bowl or cutter.
Place a tablespoon of filling on one half of each circle. Fold over and seal edges tightly with a fork.
Heat oil to 180°C (350°F). Fry pastéis in batches until golden and crispy, about 3-4 minutes per side. Drain on paper towels.
Serve immediately while hot and crispy.

title: Feijão Tropeiro
shortDescription: Traditional Minas Gerais beans with cassava flour, bacon, and eggs
note: Named after the tropeiros (mule drivers) who carried goods through the Brazilian interior
introCopy: This hearty dish from Minas Gerais combines beans, cassava flour, bacon, sausage, and eggs into a complete meal that sustained travelers on long journeys.

steps.text: In a large skillet, fry bacon until crispy. Remove and set aside, leaving fat in pan.
Cook sausage in the same pan until browned. Remove and set aside.
In the remaining fat, sauté onion and garlic until soft and golden.
Add beans and reserved cooking liquid. Bring to a simmer and cook for 5 minutes.
Push beans to the side and scramble eggs in the cleared space until just set.
Add bacon, sausage, and cassava flour, mixing everything together. The flour will absorb the liquid and create a dry, crumbly texture.
Stir in spring onions and parsley. Season with salt and pepper. Serve hot.

title: Carne de Sol com Mandioca
shortDescription: Sun-dried salted beef with fried cassava
note: A specialty of Brazil's Northeast region
introCopy: This northeastern classic pairs tender salt-cured beef with crispy fried cassava. The beef's intense flavor is balanced by the mild, starchy cassava.

ingredients.item: carne de sol or salted beef

ingredients.prepNote: peeled and cut into thick sticks

steps.text: Soak carne de sol in cold water for 2 hours to remove excess salt, changing water once. Drain and pat dry.
Boil cassava in salted water until just tender but not falling apart, about 20 minutes. Drain and let dry.
Heat butter in a large skillet and sauté onion and garlic until golden. Add beef chunks and cook, turning occasionally, until browned and tender, about 20-25 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat vegetable oil to 180°C (350°F) and fry cassava sticks in batches until golden and crispy, about 5 minutes per batch. Drain on paper towels and season with salt.
Serve beef with fried cassava, lettuce, and tomatoes. Drizzle beef juices from the pan over everything.

title: Tapioca Crepe (Sweet)
shortDescription: Naturally gluten-free tapioca crepes with coconut and condensed milk
introCopy: These chewy, naturally gluten-free crepes made from tapioca starch are a northeastern Brazilian staple. This sweet version features coconut and condensed milk.

steps.text: If using dry tapioca starch, sprinkle with a few tablespoons of water and work through a sieve until it resembles wet sand. Let hydrate for 10 minutes.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat. Sprinkle about 3 tablespoons of tapioca evenly over the pan to form a thin circle. Do not press down.
After about 1 minute, the tapioca will bind together. Sprinkle coconut over half the crepe and drizzle with condensed milk. Add a small piece of butter if desired.
Fold crepe in half and cook for another 30 seconds. Remove and serve immediately.
Repeat with remaining tapioca and filling.

title: Açaí Bowl (Brazilian Style)
shortDescription: Thick frozen açaí blend topped with granola and banana
note: Brazilian açaí bowls are thicker and less sweet than American versions
introCopy: In Brazil, açaí is served thick and barely sweetened, often eaten as a meal rather than a dessert. This energizing bowl is a staple along the coast.

steps.text: Break frozen açaí pulp into chunks. Blend with frozen bananas and coconut water until very thick and smooth, like soft-serve ice cream. Add honey if desired.
Pour into bowls immediately (it should be thick enough to hold toppings without them sinking).
Top with sliced banana, granola, coconut, and a drizzle of condensed milk if using.
Serve immediately with a spoon.

title: Quindim
shortDescription: Glossy Brazilian coconut custard with a golden top
note: A stunning dessert with Portuguese-African roots
introCopy: These jewel-like custards feature a shiny golden top and creamy coconut base. The Portuguese-influenced dessert showcases Brazil's love of coconut and egg yolks.

steps.text: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Grease 12 small muffin tins or ramekins generously with butter and dust with sugar.
Beat egg yolks with sugar until pale and thick, about 5 minutes.
Stir in melted butter, coconut milk, desiccated coconut, and vanilla until well combined.
Pour mixture into prepared tins, filling about three-quarters full.
Place tins in a bain-marie (water bath) and bake for 35-40 minutes until set and golden on top.
Cool completely, then refrigerate for at least 2 hours. Run a knife around edges and invert to unmold.
Serve chilled with the glossy golden top facing up.

title: Empadão de Frango
shortDescription: Brazilian chicken pot pie with a flaky double crust
note: A beloved comfort food across Brazil
introCopy: This impressive Brazilian pie features a rich, creamy chicken filling encased in buttery pastry. Larger than an empada, it's a centerpiece dish for gatherings.

steps.text: For the pastry, rub butter into flour and salt until it resembles breadcrumbs. Add egg yolks and enough cold water to form a dough. Wrap and refrigerate for 30 minutes.

Heat olive oil and sauté onion and garlic until soft. Add tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes. Add shredded chicken, peas, corn, cream, salt, and pepper. Simmer until thickened, about 10 minutes. Cool completely.
Preheat oven to 190°C (375°F). Roll out two-thirds of the pastry and line a 23cm pie dish.
Fill with the chicken mixture. Roll out remaining pastry and cover the pie, sealing edges well. Cut vents in the top and brush with beaten egg.
Bake for 40-45 minutes until golden brown. Let rest for 10 minutes before slicing.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Arroz Carreteiro
shortDescription: Southern Brazilian rice with charque (dried beef) and spices
note: Traditional gaucho dish from Rio Grande do Sul
introCopy: This hearty rice dish from Brazil's southernmost state combines dried beef with rice, creating a flavorful one-pot meal beloved by gauchos.

steps.text: Boil soaked charque in fresh water for 15 minutes to remove excess salt. Drain and shred finely.
Heat olive oil in a large pot and sauté onion and garlic until golden. Add bell pepper and tomatoes, cooking for 5 minutes.
Add shredded charque and cook for 5 minutes, stirring to combine.
Add rice, cumin, pepper, and bay leaves. Stir to coat rice with the mixture.
Pour in beef stock and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer until rice is tender and liquid absorbed, about 18-20 minutes.
Remove from heat and let rest, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork and stir in parsley and spring onions.
Serve hot as a main dish.

title: Casquinha de Siri
shortDescription: Stuffed crab shells with creamy crab filling and breadcrumb topping
note: Classic coastal appetizer from Bahia and Rio
introCopy: These elegant stuffed crab shells feature a rich, creamy crab mixture topped with golden breadcrumbs. A sophisticated appetizer found along Brazil's coastline.

steps.text: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Heat olive oil in a large pan and sauté onion and garlic until soft. Add bell pepper and tomatoes, cooking until softened, about 8 minutes.
Add crab meat, coconut milk, lime juice, paprika, salt, and pepper. Simmer until the mixture thickens, about 10 minutes. Stir in coriander.
Spoon the mixture into clean crab shells or individual ramekins.
Mix breadcrumbs with parmesan and melted butter. Sprinkle over each filled shell.
Bake for 15 minutes until the topping is golden and crispy.
Serve hot with lime wedges.
